CHRONICLE

THE INTRIGUES

Twenty cards. You hold one at the start and draw another whenever you play an Ace.

RULEBOOK

Put your House on the throne. Stand highest among those who did.

WHO YOU ARE

OBJECTIVE

You hold one House card and only you can read it. You also hold a Status card, 1 to 9, standing face outward. Every rival reads it, and you cannot. So you know whose side you are on, but not whether you are worth enough to lead it.

YOUR TURN

  • Play one Honor card and spend its points moving your two Emissaries along the paths. An Ace is worth one point and draws you an Intrigue.
  • The low cards carry a favour instead of movement, never both. 2 · Capture: take a rival’s Noble off the board and hold them hostage. 3 \u00b7 Exile: move a Noble to another House. 4 \u00b7 Rescue: return one of your own captive Nobles. Its captor receives an Intrigue card or advances an Emissary two spaces. The rescued Noble returns to your muster, ready to be seated again.
  • Or skip your turn entirely and take all your discards back into hand.
  • Play your whole hand and it all returns at once.
  • Own-turn Intrigues may be played before or after you move. On March replaces the Honor card altogether and lets you name the amount.

THE PATHS

  • ARMY: six spaces, allegiance.
  • CHURCH: six spaces, status. Swap your Status with a rival, discard and draw blind, force a rival to draw, or look at your own.
  • MARKET: six spaces, nobles.
  • THE HEIR’S PALADIN: eight spaces, and it pays no path action. Completing it turns the brass arrow to you, or forces a Trial by Combat if another player already holds it.

THE ARROW

While the arrow points at you, you are the Heir's Paladin: your Status counts +1, you stand among the contenders in every Call no matter which House is named, and you take the crown on any tie.

Trial by Combat. When a player completes The Heir’s Paladin while another player holds the arrow, the completing player becomes the Challenger. The Challenger and current Paladin each secretly choose one unspent Honor card from their hand and reveal simultaneously. The higher card takes or retains the arrow; the Challenger wins ties. Both cards are discarded without providing movement or using their printed abilities.

  • No current Paladin: the completing player takes the arrow without a Trial.
  • The current Paladin completes the path: they retain the arrow, and no Trial occurs.
  • A duellist with no cards in hand plays a value of 0.
  • If the Challenger completed the path using their final Honor card, the Trial is resolved before they recover their discarded hand.
  • Duel cards do not activate Capture, Exile or Rescue.
  • Neither player may recover cards in the middle of a Trial.

You may not Call for the Throne from that path.
